name: load_object_fields_into_globals
description: Copies several fields from a structure addressed by the address register into global variables, adding a fixed offset to one of them. When a count field is zero and a flag bit is clear, one stored value is negated before a further routine is called.

name: step_offset_per_frame_counter
description: Counts a frame value down and, while frames remain, calls a nested routine and moves a position value by a small amount. The amount depends on the low bit of the counter and on whether a second value's magnitude is below a threshold, and that value's sign picks the direction.

name: fill_sprite_slot_entry
description: Selects one of several 72-byte slots in a buffer using bits of a register, then stores four bytes into it: two coordinates relative to a base value, a half-scaled second coordinate with a fixed bias, and a flag byte built from bit tests on both coordinates.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: Recorded as a single instruction reached only through address-taken references, but the pseudo-code shown is a long block that copies table entries into paired structures, which does not fit that size. Its behaviour cannot be named from this evidence.

name: copy_indexed_data_to_buffers
description: When a control flag is zero and an index byte has changed, it stores the new index and toggles a buffer selector. It then clears the first longword of four destination buffers and copies longwords from two source tables into the buffers chosen by the selector.

name: advance_object_timer_state
description: On first use, marks an object as active and sets a countdown timer and a velocity, negated unless the type byte is N. Later calls count the timer down, and on expiry switch between two states, one of which initialises a second object with a velocity taken from a table.

name: poll_global_until_bit_set
description: If a global byte equals the letter p, it spins on an empty loop until that byte's top bit is set, then clears the byte to zero. Other values leave the byte untouched.

name: swap_two_global_longwords
description: Exchanges the values of two global 32-bit variables. The incoming data register is returned unchanged.

name: update_globals_with_multiword_carry
description: Masks one global longword, sets a bit, and adds the result into a second global with carry propagation. The first global is then replaced by a multiplied value, and the routine returns the second global joined with the incoming register as a 64-bit result.

name: dispatch_command_character_action
description: Reads a global command byte and branches on its letter. The letter n increments a counter and calls a routine; e calls a routine only while the counter is below thirteen; w writes several globals and calls a routine six times; s calls a routine; d sets two globals to fixed values. Other letters leave the state unchanged.

name: dispatch_on_indexed_range_match
description: When a global enable byte is zero, it selects one of sixteen range tests by a global index and checks a value against it. A value inside the chosen range sets two global flags and calls a routine. The ranges differ per index, and the last index uses its own bounds.

name: decrement_global_if_nonzero
description: Subtracts one from a global variable when it is not zero. A zero value is left unchanged.

name: initialize_globals_on_first_call
description: When a global byte is zero, it writes two fixed byte values into the globals and saves the frame base register in a global pointer. Otherwise it does nothing.

name: conditionally_call_function_pointer
description: If a global byte is nonzero, it resets that byte to a fixed value and updates a pointer one step past a saved pointer. It then calls the function reached through the saved pointer and returns the low data byte. If the byte is zero, the incoming low data byte is returned.

name: load_two_blocks_via_doio
description: Fills in an I/O request block twice and runs exec's DoIO for each. The first request transfers 11264 bytes from a large disk offset into a fixed address, and the second transfers 1024 bytes from offset 1024 into the same address. The routine returns zero.

name: unpack_backward_compressed_data
description: Decodes compressed data written from a high end address toward a low start address. It reads control bits, writes literal bytes returned by a routine, and otherwise copies earlier output back by a distance and length taken from routine results, stopping when the output pointer reaches the start.

name: test_upper_bits_no_effect
description: Tests whether a register has any bits above its lowest bit, then returns in both cases. The routine has no observable effect.

name: read_backward_bitstream_bits
description: Repeats a count held in a data register, and each time shifts the lowest bit out of a bit buffer. When the buffer runs empty it reloads it from memory one word earlier, placing the bit just shifted out in the top position of the new buffer.

name: stub_partial_decompilation
description: The routine is 1360 instructions long, but the pseudo-code shown is only a small check on a global flag that calls another routine and returns zero. Most of the body is missing, so its behaviour cannot be named from this evidence.

name: program_blitter_with_busy_wait
description: Adjusts two global offsets by a sign-dependent step and a shift of a value, then waits until a busy flag clears. It writes mask, modulo, size and control values into the blitter registers, waits again, and computes another address from the second offset.

name: blit_indexed_glyph_at_position
description: Subtracts 32 from the input register to get a table index, then computes the address of that entry in a table of 60-byte records. It waits for the blitter between each of several blit operations that place the entry's rows at positions derived from two globals, moving the position by a sign-dependent amount.

name: blit_indexed_glyph_variant
description: The decompiled body is identical to the previous entry, so this description relies on the register list. It computes a table entry from the input register the same way and programs the blitter's source, destination, modulo, size and mask registers to draw it.

name: parse_text_control_codes
description: Walks a null-terminated string one byte at a time. A space moves the position by a fixed amount, a carriage return doubles the position and adds 15, and the negative codes read a following byte as an operand to set or add to the position. Any other character advances the position by a value looked up through a routine result.

name: walk_text_string_positions
description: Another copy of the same string-walking loop, handling spaces, carriage returns, negative operand codes and table-based advances. It also contains a call to an empty routine, and its character handling otherwise matches the previous entry.

name: walk_text_string_fragment
description: A five-instruction fragment of the string-walking loop. It handles a carriage return by doubling the position and adding 15, a space by setting a width of 16, and then jumps back into the loop, so it has no standalone behaviour.

name: set_position_from_operand_byte
description: A five-instruction fragment of the string-walking loop that starts by loading one operand byte as the new position value, then continues the loop for further characters.

name: add_operand_byte_to_position
description: A five-instruction fragment of the string-walking loop that adds the following operand byte to the current position, then continues the loop.

name: add_operand_byte_and_walk
description: A five-instruction fragment of the string-walking loop that adds the following operand byte to the current position, entered from a different negative code than the previous fragment, and then continues the loop.

name: compute_blitter_shift_counts
description: Scans six words in turn for the first word with bit 0 set and separately the first with bit 1 set, each defaulting to minus one when none is found. It then shifts a global value left once for each index and clears another global, matching a blitter shift setup.

name: blit_rows_with_pointer_step
description: Waits for the blitter to be idle, then for each unit of the input count loads a source and a destination pointer into the blitter and advances both pointers by the same step.

name: set_blitter_full_copy_control
description: Writes two all-ones values to the blitter's first and last word masks, zeros the modulo and shift registers, and writes a control value that selects the blitter's channels. It sets up a full-width copy with no shift.

name: start_blit_to_destination_pointer
description: Waits for the blitter to be idle, sets full masks and a control value, then writes a destination pointer taken from an address register and a size taken from the data register, starting the blit.

name: start_blit_from_two_pointers
description: Waits for the blitter to be idle, sets full masks and a control value, then writes a source pointer, a destination pointer and a size from its inputs, starting the blit.

name: blit_four_bitplane_rows
description: If the low nine bits of the input are nonzero, it starts four blits into four bitplanes spaced by a fixed stride, using one of two modulo settings chosen by bit 9. Otherwise it starts four blits with the other fixed settings. The routine returns a value derived from the input.

name: stub_partial_decompilation
description: The pseudo-code shows only three assignments, but the routine is 149 instructions long and touches blitter, colour and DMA registers. Most of its behaviour is missing from the evidence, so it cannot be named more precisely.

name: wrap_single_routine_call
description: Calls one unnamed routine and then performs a self-assignment with no effect, so it acts only as a thin wrapper around that call.

name: build_four_entry_pointer_table
description: Writes a table of four entries by splitting a 32-bit base value into high and low words for each one, stepping the value by a global increment between entries. A conditional adds a fixed offset to the base first. Several other routines run beforehand.

name: select_masks_build_pointer_table
description: Chooses among a few preset mask values by testing globals, waits while a global is zero, then fills a four-entry pointer table the same way as the neighbouring routine and sets a colour register.

name: update_wrapped_position_record
description: Subtracts offsets from a position record and derives a small step from the low nibble of each speed field, limited to a magnitude of 32. It wraps the new horizontal and vertical positions by remainders of 304 and 224 and stores an index combining them.

name: run_counted_loops_by_flags
description: Calls a setup routine, then runs one of several counted loops depending on which of four globals is nonzero. The first case calls another routine and runs 19 outer steps of 15 inner calls, while the other cases run shorter counted loops of calls.

name: lookup_doubled_table_value
description: Takes the upper bits of a global value, scales them by two to form a byte offset, and reads a word from a fixed table at that offset. The word is doubled and stored back into the global.

name: compute_aligned_record_offset
description: Multiplies a 16-aligned value by 38 and adds it to a field of an input record, plus a fixed bias of 7904. The sum is then aligned down to a 16-unit boundary and stored in the global.

name: start_row_blits_offset_up
description: If a global flag is set, it adds 608 to a base position, then stores the base and calls a routine 19 times. It waits for the blitter and starts four blits, advancing source and destination pointers by 1043 after each one. One of two second pointers is picked by a bounds comparison.

name: start_row_blits_offset_down
description: Like its neighbour, but when the global flag is set it subtracts 608 from the base position. It then stores the base, calls a routine 19 times, waits for the blitter and starts four blits advancing both pointers by 1043.

name: store_double_and_repeat_calls
description: Stores twice a global value into a record field, then calls a routine fifteen times in a counted loop.

name: store_offset_and_repeat_calls
description: Stores twice a global value plus 36 into a record field, then calls a routine fifteen times in a counted loop.

name: start_blits_from_row_index
description: Splits a value into a coarse index and a remainder. For a nonzero coarse index it computes two pointers from a row stride of 38 bytes, waits for the blitter, and starts four blits that advance both pointers. The blitter modulo registers are set for the transfer.

name: initialise_fixed_state_values
description: Writes a fixed set of constant values into several absolute memory locations and globals, including zeros and the address of a shared global. It sets up the initial state in one pass.

name: build_copper_list_pointer_table
description: Builds a four-entry pointer table as its neighbours do, splitting a base value into high and low words and stepping it by a global increment. The register list also shows a write to the second copper list pointer.

name: toggle_between_two_pointer_sets
description: Switches a state global between two sets of values. When the first global is not at one fixed value it writes one set of three values, otherwise it writes the other set.

name: dispatch_indexed_jump_table_call
description: Calls one handler selected by a global index through a jump table, with the index scaled by four for longword entries. The table could not be recovered, so the set of handlers is unknown, and the routine returns afterwards.

name: dispatch_jump_table_call_variant
description: Makes the same indirect call as its neighbour through the same unrecovered jump table, indexed by a global value. It also calls one other routine first, which is not shown in the pseudo-code.

name: start_conditional_blit_for_column
description: When a global flag is set, it derives a column offset and a row size from its inputs, writes blitter control and mask values, and starts a blit. A second blit is started when the computed size differs from 208.

name: start_fixed_blit_when_enabled
description: When a global flag is set, it writes an adjusted pointer from a value and a shift, waits for the blitter, sets masks and a control value, and starts one blit to a fixed destination pointer. Nothing happens when the flag is zero.

name: dispatch_second_jump_table_call
description: Calls two routines and then dispatches through a second jump table, indexed by a global value scaled by four, which could not be recovered. Its handlers are separate from those of the first table.

name: dispatch_second_table_variant
description: Has the same code as the entry before it: two calls, then an indirect dispatch through the same unrecovered jump table indexed by a global value.

name: copy_tile_rows_interleaved
description: Copies data for sixteen groups of sixteen rows from a source table into a destination buffer. Each row comes from a 32-byte entry chosen by a byte of the source, and each copied word is also written 32 bytes further along.

name: write_color_list_entry_pairs
description: Writes fixed 32-bit value pairs at offsets in a list indexed by a level number, with extra entries for lower levels. Several routines run first to set the level, and the routine returns the value one of them produced.

name: clear_matching_table_records
description: Walks a table of 26-byte records while counting down a global value. For each active record whose key matches the global value it calls a routine and clears the record's active field.

name: process_records_by_threshold_checks
description: Walks a table of 26-byte records while counting down a global value. For each active record that matches the key and passes a set of range checks, it calls a routine and clears the active field. Low key values use one set of thresholds and higher key values use another.

name: setup_masked_sprite_blits
description: Reads an object record's fields to compute screen coordinates, and a first and last word mask from the low four bits of a horizontal position. It waits for the blitter and starts four blits, one per bitplane spaced by a fixed stride. A second branch does a similar setup with different sizes, but the pseudo-code is truncated, so that branch is only partly described.

name: find_first_zero_slot_entry
description: Scans up to 32 entries of 10 bytes each, starting from a pointer held in a structure. It returns as soon as an entry's word at offset 6 is zero, and if none is zero after the scan it calls another routine.

name: clear_active_slot_entries
description: Sets full blitter masks and a control value, then walks up to 32 ten-byte entries from a structure pointer. For each entry with a nonzero word at offset 6 it calls a routine and clears that word, and a zero word ends the walk.

name: blit_four_planes_with_wrap
description: Waits for the blitter, copies a value into two fields of a record, and computes a start address and a row split from a count compared against 224. It then starts four bitplane blits per pass, each spaced by a fixed stride, and repeats while the remaining count is nonzero.

name: call_four_times_then_clear
description: Sets a global value to a fixed constant, calls one routine four times, then clears three globals to zero.

name: clear_field_in_record_table
description: Clears a 16-bit field at offset 14 in each of 32 consecutive 26-byte records, starting from a fixed address, and then zeroes a global.

name: invert_underscore_marker_byte
description: When a global byte equals the underscore character, it sets the byte to zero and then inverts it, leaving all bits set. Other values are left unchanged.

name: copy_sixteen_longwords_from_table
description: Copies sixteen consecutive longwords from a fixed source address into a global buffer, four at a time, in a counted loop of four passes.

name: stub_infinite_loop_halt
description: Contains only an unconditional loop with no exit, so calling it never returns. It is reached only through code that the disassembly marked as unreached.

name: poll_routine_until_value
description: Calls a routine repeatedly until it returns 252, unless a global flag is already set. Either way the flag is cleared before the routine returns.

name: setup_four_audio_channels
description: Points each of four audio channels at a shared buffer and sets each channel's length to one word, then writes an enable value to the DMA control register for those channels.

name: read_swapped_nine_bit_position
description: Returns the low nine bits of a global value after swapping its two bytes. The register list names the video beam position registers, so the value is probably a scan line.

name: install_interrupt_vectors
description: Disables all interrupts and clears pending requests, fills ten low-memory vector entries with a fixed value, and points four interrupt vector entries at a routine. It then writes a few interrupt enable and disable masks.

name: call_with_bit_six_set
description: Sets bit six of a global, calls a routine, clears bit six again, and then sets the global to 8. The register list shows it works with the CIA interrupt control register.

name: handle_interrupt_flag_bits
description: Checks a flag bit of a global and, when it is set, calls two routines and may set the global to 255 if a returned value exceeds 251. Afterwards it keeps only the bits set in both the current and original values, limited to the low three bits.

name: shift_keyboard_serial_bit
description: When bit three of a global is set, it shifts one serial bit through the byte in inverted form, calling routines on the bit edges, and then sets the global to 8. The register list shows the keyboard serial data register is involved.

name: run_flagged_interrupt_callbacks
description: Calls one routine when bit four of a global is set. When bit five is set it calls another routine and then calls a third routine as many times as the global value, provided its top bit is clear. It finishes by keeping only the bits set in both the current and original values, limited to bits four to six.

name: dispatch_pending_request_bits
description: Checks bits seven to ten of a global request value, clearing each set bit and calling a routine for it. When the value is zero it only keeps those bits and returns.

name: keep_bits_eleven_to_thirteen
description: Keeps only bits eleven to thirteen of a global value, clearing all other bits. The register list shows an interrupt request register is involved.

name: stub_empty_return
description: Contains only a return instruction, so calling it does nothing.

name: read_joystick_direction_state
description: Derives direction flags from the joystick port movement bits, combining the vertical direction as an exclusive-or of two bit positions. It also reads the fire button from the top bit of the second input register. When the resulting state is zero it calls one routine, and it then calls another routine in every case.

name: match_key_sequence_entry
description: Compares an input character with the next entry of a sequence table and advances an index when it matches, returning early while more entries remain. When the sequence completes it calls a routine. The letter E branch ends in a bad-instruction marker, so that branch is not fully recovered.

name: apply_letter_specific_state_changes
description: When a global is nonzero, applies a change chosen by the input letter. D inverts the global and then sets it to zero, Y and X invert it, U sets it to 32 and V sets it to 1. The register list also names the beam control register, which the shown code does not write.

name: busy_delay_store_upper_bits
description: Runs a loop of 10000 iterations, each time storing the counter masked to bits eight to eleven, so the final stored value is the last masked count. It acts as a delay loop.

name: busy_delay_store_middle_bits
description: Runs a loop of 10000 iterations, each time storing the counter masked to bits four to eleven, so the final stored value is the last masked count. It acts as a delay loop.

name: busy_delay_store_split_bits
description: Runs a loop of 10000 iterations, each time storing the counter masked to bits zero to three and eight to eleven. It acts as a delay loop, and the final stored value is the last masked count.

name: busy_delay_store_low_bits
description: Runs a loop of 10000 iterations, each time storing the counter masked to bits four to seven. It acts as a delay loop. The register list names the colour register, which this global probably shadows.

name: advance_feedback_shift_register
description: Shifts a global value left one bit and sets its lowest bit when bit 23 and bit one differ, so the value steps through a feedback shift sequence.

name: step_multiplicative_congruential_value
description: Increments a global value while it is below five, returning it to one when it reaches five. It then replaces the value with its product by 177 reduced modulo 30269.

name: format_number_as_digit_string
description: Converts a number to decimal digits by repeatedly subtracting successive values from a table until a zero entry, writing each count as a digit character into a fixed buffer. The buffer is terminated with a zero, and its leading zero characters are replaced by spaces.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: Recorded as a routine, but the decompiled code is only a bad-instruction marker. The bytes are probably a table of values used by the number formatter rather than code, so its behaviour cannot be named from this evidence.

name: set_playfield_scroll_and_dma
description: Stores its input multiplied by 448, disables all DMA channels, and sets the playfield control registers to zero or fixed values. It calls a routine and then enables the DMA channels in its mask.

name: build_six_entry_pointer_table
description: Stores a base value in a structure and derives a step from the input nibbles, adjusted by fixed offsets. It then writes six 32-bit entries stepping by that value, each split into high and low words.

name: move_and_clear_table_blocks
description: Copies 32 words from one fixed table to another and clears the source, then moves 256 words from a global buffer into two other tables while zeroing the source. It clears a further block and finishes by setting a global to 30.

name: clear_fixed_word_block
description: Zeroes 544 consecutive words from a fixed address and then sets a global to 30.

name: fill_word_tables_from_routine
description: Fills 32 words at a fixed address with values returned by a routine, then fills two 256-entry tables from routine results, writing each entry into both. Finally it sets a global to 30.

name: compute_grey_level_color
description: Adds the three nibbles of an input value to a signed offset and clamps the total to 47. It then divides by three and multiplies by 273 to make a grey value from that level, masked by a second input.

name: fill_paired_routine_tables
description: Decrements a counter global and fills table entries from routine results. When bit zero of the counter is clear it fills 256 entries in two tables 512 bytes apart. Otherwise it fills 32 entries in one table and 256 entries in another, writing each value into two places.

name: stub_partial_decompilation
description: The pseudo-code shows only a return, although the routine is recorded as 31 instructions. The decompiled body does not match the recorded size, so its behaviour cannot be confirmed from this evidence.

name: call_routine_for_nonzero_bytes
description: Walks four bytes starting at an offset from a global base. For each nonzero byte it calls a routine, and the routine returns the last value it produced.

name: scan_table_for_nonzero_entry
description: Scans up to four table entries spaced 148 bytes apart, looking for a nonzero first longword. Whatever it finds, it returns the incoming data register unchanged, so the scan has no visible result.

name: advance_four_counters_with_wrap
description: When the flag global is nonzero, increments four 16-bit counters. When the first counter passes 63, it sets bit seven of the flag, resets all four counters to zero and clears the flag.

name: decode_five_bit_flags
description: When the global is zero, reads a byte from a stream pointer. A byte with its top bit set makes the global minus one. Otherwise, once a repeat counter matches, the routine advances the stream and stores minus one or zero for each of the low five bits of the byte.

name: initialise_stream_marker_state
description: Writes the byte value 255 to the address in an address register, points the stream pointer one byte past it, zeroes the stream counter and clears a global.

name: load_cia_timer_a_value
description: Writes the two bytes of its input value into the first CIA's timer A low and high registers, and sets a control global from a masked value. The timer count controls how long until the next timer event.

name: load_cia_b_timer_value
description: Writes the two bytes of its input value into the second CIA's timer A low and high registers, and sets its control register and interrupt control register.

name: call_routine_over_word_sequence
description: Loops over a count held in a structure, calling a routine with each value and incrementing a global counter. Values start from a longword in the structure, or from a second longword when the first is negative, and step by two.

name: draw_object_plane_blits
description: Waits for the blitter, sets its masks and size, and derives two screen words from record fields and the current value. It stores those words in two buffers, and when a value is nonzero it starts further blits for the plane rows. The pseudo-code is long, so this is a partial summary.

name: refresh_changed_display_digits
description: Refreshes a display's digit characters when its value changes, calling a routine for each character that differs from the stored copy. It then clamps two counts to limits of three and four and updates the display state from them.

name: copy_interleaved_byte_quads
description: Copies eleven groups of four bytes from a source to a destination, writing the first two bytes at offsets zero and two and the other two at offsets 436 and 438.

name: wait_blitter_then_start_copy
description: Waits for the blitter to be idle, then writes two pointer-derived values and a size of 1857 to the blitter registers.

name: stub_partial_decompilation
description: The pseudo-code shows only clearing a global and waiting on it, but the routine is 158 instructions long and calls 18 routines. Most of its behaviour is missing from the evidence, so it cannot be named more precisely.

name: advance_counter_and_call_routines
description: Returns early when a global is nonzero. Otherwise it calls routines depending on the global's sign, increments the global, sets it to 4095 in one path, and clears it after calling three routines.

name: initialise_game_state_values
description: Clears 3432 consecutive words from a fixed address, calls one routine, and writes a set of starting values to globals. The values include small counts, limits of 500000 and 100, 70, zeros and a fixed 32-bit pattern.

name: set_all_ones_sentinels
description: Fills four global bytes and six fixed longwords with all-ones values, typically a sentinel for empty entries.

name: program_blitter_after_calls
description: Calls three routines, waits for the blitter to be idle, then writes full masks, a control value of 496 and two more values to its registers.

name: round_position_up_sixteen
description: Calls two routines, then sets a group of globals depending on whether a global is zero or equal to another. In one branch it rounds a value up to a multiple of sixteen and subtracts eight, stores the result and clears several globals.

name: clear_twenty_one_globals
description: Sets twenty-one global variables to zero in sequence.

name: set_three_conditional_triplets
description: Zeroes four globals, then in three checks, when a global is nonzero, sets it to 255 and loads two fixed small values.

name: run_state_machine_step
description: Runs one step of a state machine on a global state value, calling routines depending on the state and returning a 16-bit value taken from the state. The pseudo-code is long and partly unresolved, so only the broad flow is described.

name: clamp_fixed_point_velocity
description: Nudges a fixed-point velocity global by a small increment, subtracts a constant step under a sign test, and clamps the result to a floor value. Which step and floor apply depends on a state byte, and one branch calls a further routine.

name: update_movement_state_offsets
description: Adjusts a movement state byte, then updates a position offset by a constant that depends on the state. Some values are clamped to 150 or 50, and one branch calls a routine.

name: step_position_by_state_offset
description: Advances a state byte by four, then subtracts a state-dependent fixed offset from a position value. When the position would leave its range, the state is set to four and the position is kept inside the limits.

name: step_position_offset_up
description: Advances a state byte by eight and adds a state-dependent fixed offset to a position value. The position is clamped within a range, and the state is set to eight when it leaves that range.

name: update_state_with_speed_limit
description: Clears a global when a state byte is zero. For nonzero states it either sets two fixed values and returns, or, when the value's magnitude is within three, increments it, and otherwise adjusts a doubled term when the high bit is clear.

name: advance_position_with_clamp_fifteen
description: Adds a fixed offset of 40960 to a value, takes its high word and clamps it to 15. Depending on the result it resets a global or sets two fixed values, then returns.

name: call_mode_routines_then_flag
description: Calls routines depending on whether bits eleven and twelve of a global match a pattern, calls two more routines, and sets a global to 96 when a flag check passes.

name: step_toward_target_within_eight
description: Returns the low bits of a value masked with five. If the difference to a target is within eight units, it moves a global toward that target by the difference; otherwise it clears the global.

name: update_mode_state_with_clamp
description: Runs a state-driven update that clamps a value to fifteen in each direction, looks up mode-based values from the upper bits, and sets several fixed values depending on the state. It calls several routines and returns early for some states.

name: update_offset_clamped_three
description: Adds a fixed offset of 5462 to a value, clamps its high word to plus three on the positive side and minus fifteen on the negative side, doubles it, and calls routines before and after. It clears a global when a flag is set.

name: update_offset_clamped_two
description: Adds a fixed offset of 3280 to a value, clamps its high word to plus two on the positive side and minus fifteen on the negative side, doubles it, and calls routines before and after. It clears a global when a flag is set.

name: call_six_routines_clear_flag
description: Calls six routines in sequence with small global assignments between them, and clears a global when a value is nonnegative and a flag is set.

name: step_toward_target_limited
description: Moves a global toward a target value. A difference of 22 or more is closed by half of its magnitude, while smaller differences are closed in one step with a sign-dependent limit. The decompiled code contains an endless loop on one negative difference, so that path is not fully recovered.

name: call_then_store_register_words
description: Calls one routine and then writes two input register words into the same global variable in turn, ending with the second.

name: store_two_register_words_variant
description: Matches the previous entry: it calls one routine and then writes two input register words into the same global variable in turn.

name: subtract_and_correct_sign
description: Subtracts a register value from a global. If the result is negative and passes a magnitude test, it corrects the result by adding twice the register value. The global is then set to 1.

name: add_with_correction_two
description: Adds a register value to a global. If the sum is non-negative and passes a comparison test, it corrects the result by subtracting twice the register value. The global is then set to 2.

name: subtract_clamp_state_four
description: Subtracts a register value from a global. When the result is negative, it clamps the high word to a small negative range and adds the register value back in one branch. In all cases it sets a state global to four.

name: add_clamp_state_eight
description: Adds a register value to a global. When the sum is non-negative and passes a bound check, it clamps the value and sets a state global to eight.

name: damp_value_toward_zero
description: Applies a damping step to a global velocity. When it is zero the routine returns early; otherwise it moves the value toward zero by up to fifteen units, with direction chosen by a bit test. The entry is recorded as three instructions, but the decompiled code is much longer, so the boundary may be wrong.

name: damp_value_toward_zero_variant
description: Matches the damping step of its neighbour. It first tests a global against a threshold and returns early when it is zero, then moves the value toward zero by up to fifteen units, with direction chosen by a bit test.

name: damp_value_fifteen_step
description: Moves a global toward zero by up to fifteen units, choosing the direction from a bit test on the result. It has no threshold check before the step.

name: add_clamped_offset_fifteen
description: Clamps a 16-bit input to the range minus fifteen to fifteen, then adds it to a global.

name: check_threshold_return_pair
description: When a global is zero and a flag is clear, it compares a value against a threshold of 12288 on either sign, calls a routine when the test passes, and returns the global together with a 16-bit result word.

name: move_by_capped_steps
description: When the state global equals one, it moves a position global in steps of 8192 toward or away from a zero point. The number of steps is capped at four or three depending on a sign test.

name: test_small_window_no_effect
description: Tests a global against a small window and returns in both branches, so the routine has no effect.

name: scan_table_for_matching_entry
description: Scans up to 32 entries of a table for one whose first word matches a derived key, stopping early at a sentinel of minus one. On a match it updates a counter in the entry, calls routines and sets two global values.

name: increment_indexed_counter_entry
description: Clears a global, sets another to 255, calls a routine, then increments the byte at a fixed table address indexed by the global.

name: update_position_toward_target
description: Updates a position and velocity pair. When the difference to a target is within 305 units it steers the value toward the target with limits, otherwise it eases toward a fixed reference point. Some frame-type values are handled specially, and a routine is called as part of the update.

name: update_position_toward_target_narrow
description: Moves a value toward a target when the difference is within 209 units, limiting the step by a bound of 200. Otherwise it eases the value toward a fixed reference by subtracting 128 and 115 and a clamped term.

name: advance_table_chain_twice
description: Twice, while the global is nonzero, adds an entry from a byte table indexed by the global to the global and then decrements it, which follows a chain through the table. The recorded size is larger than the code shown.

name: scan_entries_and_return_value
description: Sets up a few globals. When the state is zero it scans a table of 20-byte entries until one has a negative first word, calling routines per entry and returning a value. Otherwise it calls routines and returns a combined value.

name: set_state_constants_when_negative
description: When a state global is zero and negative, it sets a few state globals to fixed values, mostly by stage number, and returns. The recorded size is three instructions, but the decompiled code is larger, so the boundary may be wrong.

name: set_state_constants_variant
description: Matches the previous entry: when a state global is zero and negative, it sets state globals to fixed values.

name: reset_state_to_defaults
description: Sets state globals to fixed defaults such as 172 and 255 and decrements a counter. In one branch the first state global is set to a large fixed value.

name: set_state_seven_defaults
description: When a state global is not seven, sets it to seven and loads a fixed offset of 224 plus a constant into a position global. It then clears a global and marks the state with 255.

name: set_position_constant_by_flag
description: Sets a position global to one of two fixed values depending on whether a flag is zero, then clears a global.

name: set_negative_constant_then_clear
description: Writes a fixed large negative value to a global, then clears it to zero.

name: advance_state_by_large_step
description: When a state global is zero and a difference is nonnegative, adds 500000 to a global unless it already equals four, then adds one more step. When the state is nonzero it sets the state to four.

name: run_state_transition_table
description: A large state-transition routine that chooses among several state codes, sets a global from a state, calls routines, and then steps through a table of entries until a negative value. The decompiled flow is partly unresolved, so only its outline is described.

name: resolve_relative_table_entry
description: Steps a table index back by one and reads a 16-bit relative entry from a table. While the entry is negative it steps back or resets the index, then returns the table base plus that entry.

name: lookup_tile_flags_at_position
description: Indexes a fixed table with the high bits of a position to find a tile word. If the word has high flag bits set, it reads a shift-and-mask value from a second table and adjusts the result, then checks a neighbouring word.

name: lookup_tile_word_with_links
description: Finds a tile word from a position using a fixed index table, then follows one or two linked neighbouring words while their top flag bits are set, and stores the result.

name: step_toward_target_masked
description: Masks a global to its low 15 bits, then moves it toward a target value. A difference of 22 or more is closed by half its magnitude with a limit, and smaller differences are closed in one step. The recorded size is larger than the code shown.

name: move_by_half_step_limit
description: Returns when the input is above 21. Otherwise it moves a global by the input, using half the input for steps that would pass the current value, with sign-dependent limits.

name: add_register_to_global
description: Adds an input register value to a global variable and returns.

name: subtract_half_limited_step
description: Subtracts a register value from a global. It uses half of a second input instead when that half does not exceed the first value.

name: subtract_register_from_global
description: Subtracts an input register value from a global variable and returns.

name: stub_partial_decompilation
description: The pseudo-code shows only a return, although the routine is recorded as 17 instructions. The body is missing from the evidence, so its behaviour cannot be confirmed.

name: stub_partial_decompilation_b
description: The pseudo-code shows only a return, although the routine is recorded as 24 instructions. The body is missing from the evidence, so its behaviour cannot be confirmed.

name: stub_partial_decompilation_c
description: The pseudo-code shows only a return, although the routine is recorded as 11 instructions. The body is missing from the evidence, so its behaviour cannot be confirmed.

name: return_inverted_masked_input
description: Returns the bitwise inverse of an input register, masked to bits two and three.

name: reflect_global_when_flagged
description: Calls a routine, then when the input has any of bits 15, 14, 12, 11 or 10 set and a second routine returns nonzero, sets a global to minus three minus its value.

name: reflect_global_from_three
description: Stores an input word in a global, and when any of bits 15, 14, 12, 11 or 10 of the input is set and a second routine returns nonzero, sets the global to three minus its value.

name: compute_status_flags_from_state
description: Tests state bits of a global to decide which branch to take, adjusts a position, calls routines to compute flags, and returns a status value. The pseudo-code is long and partly unresolved, so only the outline is described.

name: check_pattern_and_set_state
description: Checks an input word against a mask pattern, with the pattern depending on whether a global is zero. On a match it sets two globals to fixed values and returns one, otherwise it returns zero.

name: process_active_entries_in_table
description: Walks 32 entries of 40 bytes each, counting entries whose code byte lies outside a small range and processing active ones with routine calls. Afterwards it may dispatch through a jump table that could not be recovered.

name: scale_byte_field_by_64
description: Returns the byte at offset one of a structure, multiplied by 64.

name: clear_two_globals_partial
description: Clears two globals, then the decompiled flow reaches a bad-instruction marker, so the rest of the routine is not recovered.

name: build_sprite_record_with_flip
description: Builds one entry in a sprite record list. It optionally mirrors the horizontal position about a width of 320, computes positions and clipping amounts, stores them in the record fields, and advances the list pointer by 26 bytes. It returns minus one when the pointer test fails.

name: build_sprite_record_variant
description: Matches the sprite record builder before it: it optionally mirrors the horizontal position about a width of 320, computes positions and clipping amounts, stores them in the record fields, and advances the list pointer by 26 bytes. It returns minus one when the pointer test fails.

name: process_entries_in_screen_window
description: Walks a table of three-word entries until one has a negative first word. For entries not yet marked done that lie inside a window around a reference value, it marks them done and calls routines chosen by the entry's type word.

name: offset_record_position_by_size
description: Adjusts a record's horizontal and vertical positions by fixed offsets derived from two size fields, unless a flag bit is set. When a mode field is not one, it calls a routine and stores a masked input word in a field.

name: allocate_free_record_slot
description: Searches 32 records of 40 bytes each for one whose first byte has its top bit set, marking it free. The found record is initialised from the input words and a type byte taken from a table, and its kind is set to 4 or 8 depending on a flag bit. Nothing happens when no slot is free.

name: allocate_slot_with_pointer
description: Performs the same free-slot search as the previous entry, and also stores a 32-bit pointer from an address register in the record it initialises.

name: offset_record_position_variant
description: Matches the record position update of the earlier entry: it applies the same size-based offsets and, when the mode field is not one, calls a routine and stores a masked input word.

name: update_active_records_loop
description: Loops backwards over 32 records and updates each active one according to its type by calling routines and setting state globals. After the loop it looks up a tile word for one final position and sets a state global. The routine is long, so this is an outline.

name: select_record_animation_frame
description: Looks at a record's flag word. When bit eight is set it adjusts the vertical position, sets two state bytes from the sign of a global, and returns. When bit seven is clear it sets a field to twelve. Otherwise it stores a frame code made from the low five bits of the flag word plus 54016.

name: set_record_frame_code
description: Chooses a value from two flag bits of a record: 5 or 11 when bit eight is clear, and 6 when it is set. It writes a fixed frame word into the record in two of the three cases, then sets each of four following fields to the chosen value when that field is nonzero.

name: set_size_globals_from_field
description: Sets two globals to 32, then when a byte field is nonzero sets them to 16 and to the field value shifted left by four.

name: update_record_contact_state
description: Updates a record's contact state from two of its flag bits. It adjusts timer-like fields and sets global states, returning early in some cases. When a range check passes it stores a value derived from the record's position.

name: check_record_range_and_store
description: Checks whether a record lies within a range of a reference value and, if it does, clears a global, sets a timer-like field to 10 when appropriate, and stores a position-derived value.

name: update_record_sprite_list
description: Updates a record's sprite list after a range check against a reference value, writing up to seven attached sprite parts into a shared buffer at a fixed address. It returns early when the record's pointer is empty. The pseudo-code is truncated, so this outline is partial.

name: update_record_sprite_list_variant
description: Matches the sprite list update of the previous entry: it writes parts of a record's sprite list into a shared buffer after a range check, in a loop of up to seven parts. The pseudo-code is truncated.

name: write_record_sprite_parts
description: When a record's position value is at least 131, writes up to six sprite part values from the record into a shared buffer, selecting the layout from a type byte. It clears the record's pointer when that pointer has no data.

name: free_or_write_record_sprites
description: Checks a record's pointer and a range value. When the record is out of range it either frees the record by clearing its first word, or writes its sprite part values into a shared buffer depending on a layout byte. It returns early when the record is still in range.

name: dispatch_record_code_events
description: Reads a code byte from a record and updates a set of counters or states according to that code, with a separate branch for each of several specific codes. It then looks up a value from a table, checks a few large constants, and decrements a global.

name: store_byte_after_call
description: Calls one routine, then stores the incoming byte in a record field at offset 24.

name: allocate_record_and_copy_parts
description: Finds the first free record in a table of 32 entries and initialises it from its inputs. It then copies up to eight sprite part values from a shared buffer into the record, stopping at a zero or a terminator of 55, and sets a state byte to show how many were copied.

name: stub_empty_return
description: The pseudo-code is only a return, so calling it does nothing. The recorded size of seven instructions is larger than that, so the body may not be fully captured.
